walkthroughs.body_html:
Measurement & Analysis — a core area of Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Measurement & Analysis brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Measurement & Analysis.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

Why does the colour of a transition metal complex change when ligands are exchanged?
options: Atoms get bigger down a group because nuclei swell when they have more neutrons.
The colour changes because the metal ion itself changes oxidation state.
The colour changes because the new ligand is itself coloured.
Different ligands cause different amounts of d-orbital splitting, so different wavelengths of light are absorbed.

mcqs.q: What is the purpose of a salt bridge in an electrochemical cell?
options: The salt bridge carries electrons between the two electrodes.
Atoms get bigger down a group because nuclei swell when they have more neutrons.
It completes the circuit by allowing ions to flow between the half-cells, maintaining electrical neutrality.
The salt bridge prevents the solutions from reacting with each other.

mcqs.q: Why does atomic radius increase down a group?
options: Atoms get bigger down a group because nuclei swell when they have more neutrons.
Each successive element has an additional electron shell, increasing the distance of outer electrons from the nucleus.
The salt bridge prevents the solutions from reacting with each other.
Atoms get bigger down a group because they have more protons attracting more matter.
